newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel PM calls for probe of corruption charges.
newsitem.headline: Israel PM calls for probe of corruption charges.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called on Friday for a police investigation into charges of corruption in his cabinet's short-lived appointment of an attorney general.
Police said they would decide on Sunday whether to look into the allegations. The politician at the heart of the controversy, Aryeh Deri, welcomed Netanyahu's call.

State-owned television alleged the attorney general's appointment was part of a deal to help Deri, who is on trial for corruption, in return for support from Deri's party for a government accord with the PLO on the West Bank town of Hebron.
"I propose a quick and thorough police investigation to reach the truth of the matter as quickly as possible," Netanyahu's office quoted him telling the cabinet.

Channel One television said on Wednesday that Roni Bar-On was appointed attorney general two weeks ago at the behest of Deri, the ultra-Orthodox ex-cabinet minister on trial on corruption charges, whose Shas party is a key coalition member.
The television alleged Bar-On promised Deri a plea bargain, enabling him to continue his political career, in return for Shas giving Netanyahu vital support for the Hebron deal.
Bar-On resigned within 12 hours of taking office under public criticism he was unfit for the job. Bar-On, Deri and Netanyahu all denied the television charges.
"I was astonished when I heard these allegations. To the best of my knowledge they have no foundation," Netanyahu was quoted as saying.
Deri told Israel's Channel Two Television he welcomed an investigation.

"I think that in the situation that has been created there has to be some sort of investigation for the public's sake and I am happy the prime minister has requested the police investigate and I hope the police will investigate and very quickly bring out the truth," he said.

"Regarding a lawsuit, I have already hesitated over the issue for two days. I will tell you the truth, perhaps it is not nice to say, a politician does not usually say such a thing: I don't have the strength for it."
Police spokeswoman Linda Menuhin said opposition legislator Yossi Sarid and Israel's Movement for Quality Government had requested an investigation and a decision would come on Sunday.
Sarid, of the left-wing Meretz party, told Israel Radio on Thursday: "We are talking about the largest corruption scandal in the history of the state if the story is correct".
Legal analyst Moshe Negbi told Israeli army radio: "If this is correct...it is an attempt by criminals or apparent criminals to control the criminal justice system."
Channel One reporter Ayala Hasson, who broke the story, insisted her information was water-tight but declined to disclose her sources.
"We wouldn't raise information like this if we weren't convinced from all directions," she told army radio.
